cues.text: What does it mean for something to be mutable?
At first, the answer seems obvious.
Something is mutable if it can be changed.

cues.action: Insert an expression before the bridge
cues.text: A sentence can be revised. A paragraph can grow. A document can be rewritten.

cues.action: The entity range follows the growing line
cues.text: And, as we have seen, even the semantic structures associated with a text can persist as that text changes.
But perhaps mutability can mean something more.

cues.action: Add two readings to the same words
cues.text: A text can acquire new meanings without being rewritten.
A document can acquire new ways of being read without losing its original composition.

cues.action: Gather the mentions, then open the gap again
cues.text: Follow Brooklyn Bridge through this little document. The passages that mention it draw together. Open the document again, and the river returns to its old place.

cues.action: Carry both interpretations back into the passage
cues.text: Sometimes, what changes is what we can do with it, how we understand it, or how it is presented to us.
We are accustomed to thinking of digital objects in terms of their categories.
An image is something we view. A video is something we play. A document is something we read and edit.
These distinctions are useful.
But must they also determine the limits of what those objects can become?
What if an image could acquire some of the capabilities of a document?
What if a conversation could become an intellectual workspace?
What if the boundaries between these categories were more permeable?
In Mutable, the block is a fundamental unit of composition.
A block may contain text, an image, a video or a more elaborate intellectual structure.

cues.action: Move pieces into two titled documents
cues.text: A document is an arrangement of such blocks.
But a block need not be permanently defined by the document in which it happens to reside.

cues.action: Seat it within the second document
cues.text: Here the photograph leaves the field notes. There is a place for it in a study of the crossing.
Its context can change without its nature necessarily changing.
We can assemble individual objects into a larger intellectual whole.

cues.action: Pull each block into its own space
cues.text: But we can also recover the constituent parts of that whole.
Composition need not be a terminal operation.

cues.action: Nest that pair with a third note
cues.text: Watch the photograph and its caption. For a moment they travel together. Open that group and each is available on its own again.
The same material can participate in new structures as our intellectual purposes change.
Consider an image.

cues.action: Assemble the research slips beside it
cues.text: This glass negative was published by the Detroit Publishing Company in nineteen oh two. Where shall we keep that fact, and our own reading of the picture?
Rather than treating those materials as a separate document, we can compose them with the image itself.

cues.action: Draw a two-face enclosure and turn
cues.text: By giving the image another surface, we create a richer intellectual object.
The reverse side can contain the apparatus through which we investigate and understand the image.
Yet the original image remains an image.

cues.action: Separate the border slightly from the print
cues.text: It has become something more without ceasing to be what it was.

cues.action: Distinguish the image from its sleeve
cues.text: The important thing is not simply that an image can be turned over.

cues.action: Place the paragraph in the same sleeve
cues.text: It is that the operation need not belong exclusively to images.

cues.action: Turn the paragraph, then the cable drawing
cues.text: A paragraph can acquire another surface. So can a drawing carried by an image block.
We need not independently invent the same capability for every kind of object.
Different objects can participate in the expressive possibilities of a common compositional system.

cues.action: Set the letter on the table
cues.text: Mutability can also operate at the scale of a single thought.
In this letter, disappointment, hope and generosity would each sound different to the person receiving it.

cues.action: Try hope, then generosity in its place
cues.text: Ordinarily, choosing one formulation means displacing another from the visible document.

cues.action: Restore the three expressions and gather them
cues.text: But the alternatives can themselves become part of the composition.

cues.action: Give them authored tabs at the decision
cues.text: We can preserve them in the very place where the creative decision is being made.

cues.action: Reread the letter with a different choice
cues.text: The document can contain not only what we have chosen to say, but also the possibilities we have considered.
As our thinking develops, the material surrounding an idea can become increasingly rich.

cues.action: Thread five contributions into the sequence
cues.text: Here the question is what draws the eye across the water. We accumulate evidence, qualifications, objections and possibilities.
Each may deserve a place in our intellectual work.

cues.action: Let the conclusion slip down the growing page
cues.text: But if everything must occupy the same continuous sequence, that richness can come at the expense of clarity.
Must everything that belongs to a document also belong to its primary reading sequence?
We can place an idea beside another idea rather than after it.

cues.action: Move the objection to the other margin
cues.text: Supporting evidence might gather on one side of an argument, and objections on the other.

cues.action: Read the main argument straight through
cues.text: Their proximity communicates a relationship without requiring them to interrupt the primary discourse.

cues.action: Reorder the observations on the left
cues.text: If we put the boats first among the observations, the balance of the reading changes again.
We are not merely arranging information for aesthetic effect.

cues.action: Leave the new reading in place
cues.text: We are using its arrangement to help us think.

cues.action: Turn the claim over to inspect the qualification
cues.text: We can also think behind an idea, preserving its supporting material on another surface.

cues.action: Give the possibility its own alternative
cues.text: We can think in alternatives, allowing several possibilities to occupy the same conceptual position.

cues.action: Move the context to its own page
cues.text: And we can think within boundaries, composing related material into manageable intellectual wholes.
Each arrangement expresses a different relationship between information and attention.
The quantity of information need not determine the complexity of its immediate presentation.

cues.action: Compare the continuous draft and the composed essay
cues.text: We have not solved the problem by discarding information.

cues.action: Trace the same coloured topics across both
cues.text: We have changed the relationships between its constituent parts.
The material remains available, but it need not all demand our attention simultaneously.
Complexity need not be eliminated.
It can be composed.
Mutability liberates spatial thinking.

cues.action: Open Field notes at its own scale
cues.text: The same principle can operate at a larger scale.
A document may be an intellectual whole in its own right.

cues.action: Bring the page into a larger study
cues.text: But that whole can also become a constituent of another composition.

cues.action: Assemble essay and source pages alongside
cues.text: Consider a research dossier made of pages. We give the photograph and its field notes a page of their own, alongside the essay and the source record.

cues.action: Enter Field notes and return to the dossier
cues.text: Step inside the field notes. We can still read the paragraph and examine the photograph separately.
Composition can operate upon the results of composition.

cues.action: Place notebook and conversation in parallel
cues.text: Conventionally, we distinguish between an application and the material upon which that application operates.

cues.action: Read the different roles of their parts
cues.text: The application is the instrument. The document is the object.
But when both participate in a common compositional architecture, that distinction can become more permeable.
The capabilities associated with one intellectual environment can become available within another.
Consider a conversation.
We might return to it not merely to remember what was said, but to investigate its ideas, identify its claims, connect its references and develop its implications.

cues.action: Add entity reference, then a gloss
cues.text: In this exchange, we can mark a reference to Brooklyn Bridge and add a gloss to the reply. The words each speaker committed stay in place.

cues.action: Hold the source wording as both readings accrue
cues.text: The conversation can become an object of sustained intellectual work without ceasing to be a conversation.

cues.action: Follow the reference across the exchange
cues.text: We need not treat dialogue as something intellectually separate from the documents through which we think.
Now consider a video. Listen to a few seconds of a lecture on reading this photograph.

cues.action: Play a voiced excerpt over a moving study of the plate
cues.text: Look at the Brooklyn Bridge. Follow the deck out over the water. The far tower nearly disappears into the sky.

cues.action: Lay out a transcript, still and reference
cues.text: We may wish to study what is said in it, examine particular images, record observations, investigate its references, or connect its ideas to our wider knowledge.

cues.action: Bring the apparatus behind the video and wrap
cues.text: These materials can become part of a composition associated with the video itself.

cues.action: Turn to the transcript and mark its entity
cues.text: A reverse surface can contain an annotated transcript.

cues.action: Visit the screenshots and the reference list
cues.text: Tabs can preserve screenshots, references and related material within the same intellectual context.
The video acquires textual, semantic and scholarly dimensions.
Yet it remains a video.
We have not merely changed its appearance.
We have extended what it can become.

title: Enrichment is not a terminal operation

cues.action: Keep the player on the table
cues.text: But even this enriched composition need not be a final destination.

cues.action: Unwrap, then release the three panels
cues.text: First we unwrap the reverse. Its contents move beside the video. Opening the tabs releases the transcript, the stills and the references in order.

cues.action: Move the transcript, then wrap a still
cues.text: We move the annotated transcript to a new research page. Its former place is empty. A still can now acquire a surface of its own.

cues.action: Place the source with the new page
cues.text: A body of research material can participate in another composition.
The objects that constitute one intellectual whole can become available for further intellectual work.
Enrichment is not a terminal operation.
An image can become more than an image.

cues.action: Switch the letter and spread the essay
cues.text: A conversation can become more than a conversation.

cues.action: Place the essay in the dossier
cues.text: A document can become part of another document.
Their capabilities need not be exhausted by their original categories.

cues.action: Turn the lecture to its transcript
cues.text: Their contexts need not determine their permanent locations.
Their present arrangements need not determine their future possibilities.

cues.action: Gather a smaller pair within another document
cues.text: Each can participate in new forms of intellectual work while retaining what makes it recognisable.
Perhaps mutability is not simply the capacity of an object to undergo change.

cues.action: Add and turn its research surface
cues.text: Perhaps it is the capacity to acquire new forms, new relationships and new possibilities without necessarily surrendering its nature.
The freedom to compose.
The freedom to decompose.
The freedom to extend.
The freedom to recontextualise.

cues.action: Set the first line of the thesis
cues.text: Mutability is not merely the freedom to change things.

cues.action: After a pause, complete the thesis
cues.text: It is the freedom to change what things can become.
Mutable.

cues.action: Reveal the slogan and hold still
cues.text: Same Thing. Many Faces.
